text:
Samsung Galaxy A54 5G Samsung Galaxy A54 5G

MSRP: $449.99

About this Samsung Galaxy A54 5G review: I tested the Samsung Galaxy A54 5G (6GB RAM, 128GB) over a period of seven days. It was running Android 13 with Samsung's One UI 5.1 skin on the March 1, 2023 security patch. Android Authority purchased the unit for this review.

## Samsung Galaxy A54 5G review: What you need to know

Ryan Haines / Android Authority

- Samsung Galaxy A54 5G (6GB/128GB): $449 / £449 / €489
- Samsung Galaxy A54 5G (8GB/256GB): £499 / €539

...

Galaxy A54 5G camera trio

The Galaxy A53 5G had four rear cameras. The Galaxy S23 has three. For the Samsung Galaxy A54 5G to adopt the flagship-inspired design, something had to give. It either had to stick with four lenses and sport a Galaxy S23 Ultra-style layout or choose one of its quartet to send off to pasture. Samsung chose the latter, but don’t let the numbers fool you: the Galaxy A54 5G is an even better budget camera phone than the Galaxy A53 5G.

Compared to its predecessor, the Samsung Galaxy A54 5G surrenders some megapixels in favor of size. The primary sensor drops from 64MP to 50MP, but the individual pixels grow from 0.8μ to a nice, even 1.0μ. It bins to 12.5MP by default, but you can toggle back to the full resolution if you wish. Accompanying the primary camera are a 12MP ultrawide lens and a 5MP macro shooter that are unchanged from the previous generation. That means Samsung’s 5MP depth sensor was the one left on the chopping block, not that you’ll notice its absence very often.

As usual, the default Samsung camera app is stuffed to the gills with features and controls, some of which are more useful than others. You can toggle from ultrawide (0.5x) up to the Galaxy A54 5G’s 10x maximum digital zoom with simple buttons, while options like Night Mode and the dedicated macro lens lie in Samsung’s More menu. There’s no telephoto lens, which means no support for Expert RAW for those into tinkering with shots on their phone, but the Galaxy A54 5G brings back what Samsung calls Fun Mode. It’s essentially a set of Snapchat-like filters that run through the main camera in case you really want to look like a giraffe without having to send the image to your friends, I guess. It’s perhaps a bit surprising that Fun Mode isn’t standard across all Samsung Galaxy A devices, as it was notably absent from the Galaxy A14 5G that I just finished reviewing.

...

Samsung has been heading away from higher megapixel count selfie cameras on its flagships, but it didn’t tell the Galaxy A54 5G. The mid-ranger still packs a 32MP punch hole shooter, which bins to 8MP by default. I’m pleased with the Galaxy A54 5G’s sharpness in both shots below, though I can’t help but notice slightly richer tones in the portrait selfie. My skin looks less washed out, and my shirt is a bit deeper blue. However, the edge detection missed a few locks of hair, specifically where it overlaps with the wooden structures behind me.

As for video, the Samsung Galaxy A54 5G comes with middling options on both front and back. You can only record 4K footage at 30fps from either side and 1080p at up to 60fps. Essentially all of the Samsung Galaxy A54 5G’s primary competitors have picked up support for 4K at 60fps at a similar price point, so doubling down on 30fps leaves this mid-ranger a bit lacking. It’s just not good enough if you’re after smooth, high-res video. If you’re itching to slow things down, the Galaxy A54 5G’s rear cameras support 720p at up to 480fps.

title: Galaxy A54 Camera in 2026: Reviewer Findings and Settings
text:
By Samsung Photography Academy Editorial Team· May 15, 2026· Updated November 6, 2026

...

The Samsung Galaxy A54 debuted with a 50MP OIS camera in March 2023 for $449 (US). Since then, Samsung has released three more Galaxy A5x series phones, the latest being the Galaxy A57 (March 2026). Chances are if you’re shopping for a Galaxy A54 today, you’ll find yourself looking at either old stock or second-hand options.

The good news is that the Samsung Galaxy A54’s 50MP OIS camera still manages to deliver. The less exciting news is that as we move further into 2026, the more pertinent question becomes how much longer Samsung will continue to support the Galaxy A54 with software updates.

Pictures taken during the day with the Galaxy A54’s 50MP main camera (with OIS) are sharp and have natural colours. GSMArena also rated the phone’s low-light shots highly. The Galaxy A54’s ultrawide and 5MP macro cameras are less impressive. The Galaxy A54 will get One UI 9 (Android 17) as its fourth and final major OS upgrade and is promised security patches for five years from its launch date. Consider buying the Galaxy A54 only at a clear discount.

## Galaxy A54 camera specs

| Camera | Hardware | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Main | 50MP, f/1.8, 23mm, 1/1.56-inch sensor, OIS | Saves 12.5MP binned photos by default, with a 50MP mode |
| Ultrawide | 12MP, f/2.2, 13mm, 123° | Fixed focus |
| Macro | 5MP, f/2.4 | Fixed focus at about 4cm |
| Front | 32MP, f/2.2, 26mm | Saves 12MP in the wide view and 8MP in the cropped view |
| Video | 4K30 on the main and ultrawide cameras, 1080p60 on the main | 4K stabilisation arrived in a software update |
| Chip and software | Exynos 1380, launched on Android 13 | Updating to One UI 9 (Android 17) |

Specs from GSMArena's A54 spec sheet and review.

## How the A54 camera performs

We don’t have an A54 to hand so can’t comment on image quality ourselves, but according to GSMArena’s review, daylight shots from the main camera are excellent, with accurate white balance, wide dynamic range and unobtrusive sharpening. Switching to 50MP adds a little detail but isn’t magic – grass, for example, still isn’t going to resolve all that well.

According to GSMArena’s review, the main camera also performs well at night. It’s worth noting that Photo mode will engage some sort of night-time processing when conditions warrant, so Night mode often won’t offer much in the way of additional benefit (at least on the 1x camera; the ultrawide produces rather washed-out colours in poor light, and GSMArena reckons Night mode only improves things a little).

There’s no telephoto camera, so tapping 2x in the camera app performs a crop from the 50MP main camera – GSMArena’s review suggests these aren’t bad at all – and anything beyond that is digital zoom. The 5MP macro camera has a fixed focus distance of around 4cm, so be prepared to get up close and personal (and watch out for casting your phone’s shadow onto your subject!). There are a couple of workarounds in the macro photography guide.

Video capture maxes out at 4K30. Stabilisation was limited to 1080p video at launch, but GSMArena has since updated its review to reflect the fact that Samsung has added stabilisation for 4K footage via a software update. Footage shot in poor lighting conditions is GSMArena’s least favourite, however, with colours looking a little washed out and highlights a touch harsh.

## Settings that suit the A54

| Situation | What to use | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Everyday daylight | 1x main camera at the default resolution | Clean files and the fastest shooting |
| Static scene you'll crop | 50MP mode in bright light | More definition when you have light to spare |
| Evening and night | Photo mode on the 1x camera, phone braced | Night processing already runs in dim scenes |
| Portraits | Portrait mode at 1x or 2x, blur turned down | GSMArena found the default blur a little strong |
| Moving subjects | Pro mode on the main camera with a fast shutter | Pro mode is available on the main camera |
| Close-ups | Macro mode at about 4cm, in good light | The macro lens can't focus any closer or further |
| Video | 4K30 or 1080p60 on the main camera | The ultrawide struggles in low light |

...

## Software updates and Galaxy AI

Samsung promised four generations of Android updates and five years of security updates for the Galaxy A54 at the time of its launch. One UI 9 with Android 17 has started rolling out in South Korea as per a report by SamMobile and has since expanded to India and other countries/regions as of early November 2026. Since this is the fourth update for the phone, you shouldn’t expect any more Android updates. However, security updates should continue till around 2028.

...

## Should you buy a Galaxy A54 in 2026?

If you can pick one up at a steep discount off the price of an A56, and you tend to take most of your pictures in daytime or at-home scenarios, it’s worth buying, as the A54’s camera is still pretty good. It also retains 2x cropping and Pro mode, both of which are carried over to newer models.

But if you want a handset that’ll stick around for four or five more years, you’ll want to look elsewhere, as the A54 has no major Android updates left, and will see an even shorter stretch of security-only support.
